label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Our Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms came to a close on Saturday, and on behalf of the organising team, I want to thank everyone who made it possible.

From 5–7 November, we welcomed 41 MSc and early PhD participants from nine states to Seminar Hall 2 at the Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. We received 112 applications and selected participants based on a statement and one reference. Seeing so many people travel to spend three days doing mathematics together was very special.

Thank you to our speakers: Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari, who joined us from Hyderabad to speak on Mordell–Weil; Dr. Sunanda Iyer from Chennai, for her sessions on modular forms; and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined us online from Kraków for computations in Sage. Thank you for making time for questions and discussions throughout the school.

One moment I particularly enjoyed was when an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma’am’s notes. She corrected it live and thanked him. That exchange captured what we hoped the school would be: a place where students feel comfortable asking questions and engaging with the mathematics.

We also had a nearly two-hour power cut on the second afternoon. As laptops died, we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It turned out to be the best session of the three days!

Thank you to our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, for her guidance; to Mr. Prakash Salunke, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when the booking got mixed up; and to the six PhD student volunteers who ran the problem sessions and helped as TAs. The PhD-led sessions worked well, and we hope to keep that format.

The institute’s student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh covered hostel stays and travel for 18 outstation students. We are grateful for that support. Thank you also to my fellow organisers, Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza, and to every participant for bringing curiosity and energy to the school.

For MSc students especially, small schools can offer something big conferences often cannot: the space to stop and ask questions. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, subject to funding. Slides and problem sheets will be shared on the department website within two weeks.
